o1.biggest_strength: Builds the whole series around the two habits the data says predict retention (recurring task plus second device), branches by signup platform, and drops the weak emails with the numbers to back each cut.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 pushes sharing a list after the owner's strongest signal was to drop the team invite, and sharing only reaches 6% of users at 34% retention, so it dilutes the two-habit focus.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace or trim email 5 so the whole series stays on the two habits, with a short, quiet closing email or no fifth email at all.

o2.biggest_strength: A calm, on-brand series with clear per-email goals and honest reasoning about the two habits, plus a nicely gated Pro email for engaged users only.
o2.biggest_mistake: It leaves the old projects-and-labels slot open and pushes Pro to day 14 without a fifth onboarding habit, so the five emails don't fully use the trigger set and the sequence has a soft end.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use all five allowed triggers to drive a fifth habit-focused email and tighten the claims and numbers so each measure traces to the data.

reason: Both are calm, on-brand and built on the right two habits, but Output 1 states the goal and success measure sooner, uses the platform branch and skip rules more precisely, and its cuts are better argued with the numbers. Output 2 is close, with a nicer gated Pro email, but its fifth slot and sequence logic are a touch weaker.
